I'm not expecting Carolina to perform like Buffalo did, but the Panthers are highly susceptible to being dragged into shootouts if their opponent starts to sling the ball around. articles.text: Bleacher Report's Expert Week 1 2026 NFL Picks Bleacher Report NFL CFB MLB NBA NHL WNBA Fantasy Football Get Our Newsletter Sports on HBO Max NFL Teams Scores Standings Draft Rumors Fantasy NFL 1000 Odds Teams Scores Standings Draft Rumors Fantasy NFL 1000 Odds nfl college football mlb nba nhl wnba fantasy football world football golf tennis wwe college basketball womens college basketball mma fiba womens basketball nascar unrivaled boxing olympics all elite wrestling formula 1 moto gp afc east buffalo bills miami dolphins new york jets new england patriots afc north cincinnati bengals cleveland browns baltimore ravens pittsburgh steelers afc south indianapolis colts jacksonville jaguars houston texans tennessee titans afc west denver broncos los angeles chargers kansas city chiefs las vegas raiders nfc east washington commanders dallas cowboys philadelphia eagles new york giants nfc north chicago bears detroit lions green bay packers minnesota vikings nfc south tampa bay buccaneers atlanta falcons carolina panthers new orleans saints nfc west san francisco 49ers arizona cardinals los angeles rams seattle seahawks 01:31 Featured Video Top Fantasy Performers 📈 Previous Next Home NFL New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (left) and Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold (right) NFL Bleacher Report's Expert Week 1 2026 NFL Picks B/R NFL Staff Sep 9, 2026 It's a new year for Bleacher Report's experts, and they're ready to lead you through another profitable season. We're back with the same crew that includes analysts Gary Davenport , Brad Gagnon , Kris Knox , Moe Moton , and Brent Sobleski , along with editors Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford . Last season, Gagnon and Hanford led the group at 143-127-2 for the season. Moton finished third at 139-131-2. Our panel will use the same format as last year, sharing all their picks and challenging each other with opposing views on every game unless there's a unanimous selection. We'll also keep track of lone-wolf picks, which were 32-29-1 last year. Now, let's look ahead to the Week 1 slate, which starts Wednesday with the Super Bowl LX rematch and a lone-wolf pick right off the top. Lines are from FanDuel as of Wednesday, Sept. 9, at 4 p.m. ET. Check FanDuel for the latest odds info. Information on public betting trends is courtesy of the Action Network . ATS records are provided by Team Rankings . New England Patriots at Seattle Seahawks 1 of 16 AP Photo/Lindsey Wasson Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba FanDuel Line: Seahawks (-3.5) Knox: Seahawks (-3.5) I don't think the Super Bowl LX rematch will be as one-sided as last year's championship game. However, I do believe Seattle's defensive front can prevent Drake Maye and the Patriots from finding an offensive rhythm once again. With home-field advantage playing a factor, Seattle should win by more than a field goal and walk away with a 1-0 record. Moton: Patriots (+3.5) It's understandable that the panel leaned heavily toward the Seahawks, given Seattle's dominant 29-13 victory over New England in Super Bowl LX seven months ago. Since then, the Seahawks have lost key parts of that team and coaching staff. Former Seahawks offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak is now the head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders. Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker, who led Seattle's backfield with 1,027 yards and five touchdowns, signed with the Kansas City Chiefs. The Seahawks also lost cornerback Riq Woolen and safety Coby Bryant in free agency. Meanwhile, the Patriots added wideouts A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Running back TreVeyon Henderson won't play because of an ankle injury, though Rhamondre Stevenson has handled a workhorse role in the past. New England covers the 3.5-point spread. Predictions Patriots: Moton Seahawks: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski San Francisco 49ers at Los Angeles Rams (in Australia) 2 of 16 AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford FanDuel Line: Rams (-3.5) Hanford: Rams (-3.5) There's no team entering the season with bigger hype than the Rams, and I'm buying it. While you could argue that their travel plans and a 49ers team that's probably more overlooked than it should be entering the season is a recipe for an upset, I think the Rams will show right away why they're the Super Bowl favorites. L.A. wins by a touchdown behind a dominant defensive performance. O'Donnell: 49ers (+3.5) Both teams have been major offseason headline generators: the Rams for building a super team headlined by the Myles Garrett trade and return of Aaron Donald; and the 49ers for what boils down to a lot of negativity headlined by injuries. In fact, while almost all the focus has been on George Kittle's potential return in Week 1, we don't actually know if Christian McCaffrey will be fit to play, and conventional wisdom would be to back the favorites. But these two teams traveled a long, long way to play a football game, and I'd rather take the points against a familiar foe in an unfamiliar setting regardless of who is on the field. Predictions 49ers: Gagnon, Moton, O'Donnell Rams: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Sobleski Buffalo Bills at Houston Texans 3 of 16 AP Photo/David J. Phillip Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud FanDuel Line: Bills (-1.5) Davenport: Bills (-1.5) Laying points on the road against arguably the NFL's best defense is starting the season with some anxiety. But I have that much more anxiety about C.J. Stroud after how he finished last season—Josh Allen leads the Bills to a close win on one of Week 1's better games. Gagnon: Texans (+1.5) Week 1 is a lot of gut, and I have a feeling the Houston defense will be extremely prepared for Buffalo in the Texans' home opener. That was certainly the case when they beat the Bills at this very site in November 2025. The Bills are an excellent team, but this is a tough spot for their new coach. Predictions Bills: Davenport Texans: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski TOP NEWS Cardinals Finalizing MHJ Trade Bleacher Report 9h Latest on MHJ Sweepstakes 👂 Bleacher Report 1h DK Shades Sauce Gardner 👀 Bleacher Report 10h Chicago Bears at Carolina Panthers 4 of 16 AP Photo/Carolyn Kaster Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams FanDuel Line: Bears (-2.5) Moton: Bears (-2.5) The Bears enter this matchup with a shaky secondary. Safety Coby Bryant underwent knee surgery and will miss a few months of action. Slot cornerback Kyler Gordon is on the physically unable to perform list with a calf injury. However, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young hasn't shown the ability to exploit opposing pass defenses' weaknesses, averaging just 180.2 passing yards per game over his three-year career. Bears go on the road with their ascending offense and win by at least a field goal. Sobleski: Bears (-2.5) The Carolina Panthers finished among the bottom six in total offense last season. The organization added next-to-nothing to improve the unit. If anything, the group might be worse since both offensive tackle spots remain a serious concern. Conversely, the Chicago Bears are explosive enough offensively to easily cover this spread. Predictions Bears: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski Cleveland Browns at Jacksonville Jaguars 5 of 16 AP Photo/Gary McCullough Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence FanDuel Line: Jaguars (-7.5) Gagnon: Jaguars (-7.5) I think the Browns could have some surprisingly nice moments this season, but this ain't the spot. Cleveland is, at the very least, a work in progress as a new core and coaching staff settle in. The Jaguars, on the other hand, are a well-oiled machine on a strong trajectory following a superb second half to the 2025 campaign. I expect them to keep rolling in their home opener. Sobleski: Browns (+7.5) Despite every expectation of the Cleveland Browns' offense imploding thanks to questionable quarterback setup, Todd Monken's squad gets the benefit of the doubt in the head coach's debut because of its defense. Myles Garrett might be gone, but this unit still has playmakers at all three levels to slow the Jaguars and make the contest interesting. Predictions Browns: Hanford, Knox, Sobleski Jaguars: Davenport, Gagnon, Moton, O'Donnell Atlanta Falcons at Pittsburgh Steelers 6 of 16 AP Photo/Gene J. Puskar Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers FanDuel Line: Steelers (-3.5) Gagnon: Falcons (+3.5) I don't trust the Steelers, and I hate that hook for them. It's really that simple. These teams are closer to being evenly matched than many might believe, and the Steelers were far from impressive at home in 2025. The Falcons didn't lose by more than a field goal in regulation in any of their last six road games last season. They should keep this game tight. Hanford: Steelers (-3.5) The jury is out on Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy's reunion in Pittsburgh and the impact it will have on a stagnant Steelers offense, but I just don't see the "winner" of the NFL's least inspiring QB battle, Tua Tagovailoa, doing serious damage to the Steelers defense. I expect this game to be ugly, like most Steelers games, but Tagovailoa makes one too many mistakes as Pittsburgh improves to 6-1 ATS in its last seven games against Atlanta. Predictions Falcons: Gagnon Steelers: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski New York Jets at Tennessee Titans 7 of 16 AP Photo/George Walker IV Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward FanDuel Line: Titans (-1.5) Davenport: Jets (+1.5) Fans who watch this entire game should receive some sort of reparations from the NFL. Neither offense in this slopfest can be trusted even a little, but for my money the Jets are slightly better defensively. First team to 13 points wins! Knox: Titans (-1.5) I'm inclined to believe it when I see it with Robert Saleh, Cam Ward, and the Titans. However, I believe they at least have the potential to turn things around quickly. The Jets? Not so much. I believe that New York is playing for 2027 and beyond. I don't envision Tennessee running away with this one, but I don't see the Jets winning on the road, and this is awfully close to a pick'em. Predictions Jets: Davenport Titans: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski New Orleans Saints at Detroit Lions 8 of 16 AP Photo/Caroline Brehman New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough FanDuel Line: Lions (-7) Hanford: Saints (+7) The Saints closed last season red hot, and while some of that may be fool's gold, I think they'll keep this one within a touchdown. I expect Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs and Co. to have success against the Saints' defense, but I don't trust the Lions' secondary to give Tyler Shough major issues. Lions win by six in a high-scoring game. O'Donnell: Lions (-7) Hey, the Saints are going to be feisty, and the panel is just about split on the Lions giving this many points for good reason. Missing the playoffs a year ago should be gnawing at Dan Campbell's group, though. Detroit scored an average of 32-plus points per game at home last season — a full touchdown more than on the road. Can the Saints go toe-to-toe in a shootout with the Lions in Detroit? Maybe, but I'll back a first-week barrage from the stronger offensive unit as the Lions look to set the tone for a rebound campaign. Predictions Saints: Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski Lions: Davenport, Gagnon, O'Donnell Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Cincinnati Bengals 9 of 16 AP Photo/Carolyn Kaster Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow FanDuel Line: Bengals (-3.5) Knox: Buccaneers (+3.5) If Joe Burrow can stay healthy, Cincinnati's new-look defense should make the Bengals legitimate AFC contenders. However, the Bengals have been notorious for slow starts under Zac Taylor. I can't envision them winning big against a Buccaneers team that can play the underdog card after missing the playoffs in 2025. Sobleski: Bengals (-3.5) Joe Burrow and Co. should hit the ground running. Can the Tampa Bay Buccaneers do the same without Mike Evans on the roster? Obviously, quarterback Baker Mayfield has other weapons in Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Jalen McMillan. However, the Cincinnati Bengals still have an advantage in offensive firepower with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, who were both back at practice this week. Predictions Buccaneers: Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell Bengals: Davenport, Gagnon, Moton, Sobleski Baltimore Ravens at Indianapolis Colts 10 of 16 AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson FanDuel Line: Ravens (-3.5) Hanford: Ravens (-3.5) Backing this many favorites at 3.5 makes me antsy, but I think the Ravens will be too much for the Colts here. I'm not sold on the Ravens overall this season, but I think their improved defense under Jesse Minter, with the addition of Trey Hendrickson, should give them enough punch to make life very difficult for Daniel Jones. Lamar Jackson has to get back on track as a passer this season, but I think he makes enough plays to put Baltimore over the top. Sobleski: Colts (+3.5) Interestingly, the Indianapolis Colts' defense has a very specific matchup in its favor, with the defensive tackle duo of DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart facing two brand-new starters along the Baltimore Ravens' offensive line. Thus, the Colts could control the line of scrimmage to make life difficult on quarterback Lamar Jackson and running back Derrick Henry. Offensively, Indianapolis should have all of its pieces back in place to get off to a hot start, as it did last season. Predictions Ravens: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Moton Colts: Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski Washington Commanders at Philadelphia Eagles 11 of 16 AP Photo/Daniel Kucin Jr. Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels FanDuel Line: Eagles (-5.5) Hanford: Eagles (-5.5) The Eagles have a lot of questions to answer on the offensive side of the ball in Week 1, but I'm just not buying the Commanders yet. Jayden Daniels is healthy, which will help, but the weapons around him leave some to be desired, and the absence of star LT Laremy Tunsil will loom large against an Eagles defense that loves to get after the quarterback. I'm not sure Jalen Hurts silences the critics in Week 1, but I do think the Eagles have enough juice in the run game and on defense to control the game and win by a touchdown. Moton: Commanders (+5.5) This is a divisional matchup, and both quarterbacks are learning new offenses. Expect both teams to be inefficient in a game of missed opportunities, while both defenses capitalize on miscues with takeaways. Philadelphia also lost some offensive explosiveness when it traded three-time Pro Bowl receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots. On the ground, running back Saquon Barkley helps the Eagles grind out a close victory by a margin short of a touchdown. I'll take the points—with exactly zero confidence. Gagnon: Vikings (-1.5) I don't know how I feel about the Packers opening the season on the road against a sneaky-good division rival without Josh Jacobs and Micah Parsons. Throw in the unpredictability factor with Kyler Murray, and I think Green Bay is in a tough situation here. Predictions Packers: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell Vikings: Davenport, Sobleski Miami Dolphins at Las Vegas Raiders 13 of 16 AP Photo/John Locher Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty FanDuel Line: Raiders (-3.5) Moton: Raiders (-3.5) According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Las Vegas Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers is expected to miss "a game or two" after undergoing a trim on his meniscus. On a positive note from the injury front, head coach Klint Kubiak is optimistic about running back Ashton Jeanty suiting up after he suffered an ankle injury during practice on August 23. Without Bowers, expect the Raiders to feature Jeanty (if healthy) and rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. on the ground, which should be enough to control time of possession. Week 1 divisional matchups can be unpredictable, and I won't be shocked if the Giants steal this one. I think it's far more likely that Dallas makes one or two defensive plays that it wouldn't have made a year ago to preserve a one-score victory. O'Donnell: Giants (+2.5) The Cowboys are the better team on paper, and the Giants' secondary will have a hard time defending CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens even if Big Blue is getting to Dak Prescott. The Chiefs will go as Mahomes does, and one or two instances of him hesitating behind the line will sink them against arguably the most well-rounded team in the conference. O'Donnell: Chiefs (-2.5) The Denver defense is going to be a problem for Kansas City, especially with a less than 100% healthy Patrick Mahomes back under center. And the Chiefs have lost two of the last three season openers, with the lone victory being a controversial end-of-game call that gave K.C. the victory over Baltimore in 2024. Yeah, all things point to a Broncos cover, if not an outright win. So, I'll ride with the minority and lay these points with the home team covering late. By Zachary Cohen - September 26, 2026 83213 X Facebook Email It’s time for Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season. I strongly suggest you check out the Week 3 NFL Betting Hub , where you’ll find all of the features and picks from my talented co-workers. On top of that, we never stop pumping out good NFL content on our live shows . That’s the beauty of being a subscriber. As a company, we’re relentless in our effort to get you prepared for these games. With that out of the way, let’s get into the fun stuff. Keep reading for my Week 3 NFL best bets and Week 3 NFL player props. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts New England Patriots at Jacksonville Jaguars – 1:00 pm ET The Jaguars are coming off a loss last week, but there’s no shame in losing to the Broncos. That was a meeting between two teams that can easily work themselves deep into the AFC playoffs. Denver just so happened to be the home team. Well, Jacksonville will be the home team in this meeting with New England, giving the Jaguars a little bit of an edge. However, beyond that, I currently view them as a better team than the Patriots. It’s very early in the season, but Jacksonville currently resides in Tier 2 when looking at RBSDM’s EPA tiers. New England is barely in Tier 3. The Patriots are undoubtedly a strong defensive team, but very little separates these teams on that side of the ball. The difference between the two is on offense, as the Jaguars have a balanced lineup and an excellent play caller. The Patriots have the latter, along with a talented quarterback, but they’re missing AJ Brown. This is the exact type of game in which that could come back to haunt them. Our VSiN matchup page for this game calls for the Jaguars to win by 3.0. I see it being a little more lopsided than that, but we have -2.5 in case it is decided by a field goal. Bet: Jaguars -2.5 (-120) Tennessee Titans at New York Giants – 1:00 pm ET It might be hard to get on board with backing the Giants without Jaxson Dart, and it’s probably harder considering how poorly Jameis Winston played against the Rams. However, we haven’t seen anything through two weeks that suggests Tennessee is better than New York. The Giants are currently last in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (0.257), but it’s early enough in the season that each game can really change stats. Well, New York got carved up by Los Angeles in the Sunday Night Football game, and this Titans offense isn’t the Rams offense. I’d be very surprised if Cam Ward can go on the road and deliver a victory — or cover 2.5 points — against a tough team with playoff aspirations. As things stand, the Titans are ranked 20th or worse in both EPA/Play and EPA/Play Allowed. I’m also not too worried about Winston. Sure, last week was absolutely miserable, but his track record as a starter speaks for itself. Honestly, a good argument can be made that he’s the best backup in the league, and a week of reps with the starters should do him wonders. His timing looked off in Week 2, and that should get there as he gets more familiar with his weapons. John Harbaugh has also been outrageously productive in games with lines between +3 and -3. In his career, his teams are 79-53 straight-up and 73-49 against the spread in those games. Bet: Giants -2.5 (-118) Ravens at Cowboys – 4:25 pm ET Henry is averaging 106.0 yards per game through two weeks, and his 144-yard performance against the Colts helped. He absolutely dominated Indianapolis between the tackles, and something tells me he’ll do the same to Dallas. In Week 1, the Cowboys gave up 165 rushing yards against the Giants. Dallas also allowed 182 rushing yards against Washington last week. As of right now, despite all the offseason moves the Cowboys made to address their defense, they’re No. 24 in the NFL in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.003). That’s trouble heading into a meeting with Henry, who can run over defenders up the middle or utilize his quickness to break off a long one. In Henry’s last 11 games against bottom-10 opponents in rushing yards allowed, the future Hall of Famer is averaging 104.1 rushing yards per game. He has also gone Over 85.5 rushing yards in six of the 11. I’ll also note that Henry rushed for 151 yards the last time he played at Jerry World. That was a different defense and venue, but he’ll enjoy the atmosphere in Brazil — and extra eyeballs. Wilson dealt with an injury that kept him out for most of last season, but in the first six games of the season when he was fit, Wilson had at least six catches in four of those six games. Geno Smith did not have a good season in Las Vegas, but he had a terrible offensive line and a bad group of skill position players. He might not get back to the guy he was in Seattle, but he should have a much better season with an underrated Jets offensive line protecting him. This is a good early matchup for Smith to get his feet under him in a Jets uniform (for the second time) and feed his WR1 Garrett Wilson. He only played nine games in his rookie season for the Chargers, but he is set for a huge role in what should be a productive Los Angeles offense. This is a good matchup for him to start the season against the Cardinals. Last season, Arizona ranked 22nd in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 23rd in defensive rushing success rate. That defense has a lot of young, inexperienced pieces and should struggle again this season. The Chargers should feed the ball to Hampton early and often to control the game against Arizona. The Chargers are also big favorites and should lead this game down the stretch. That should lead to a lot of carries for Hampton down the stretch while the Chargers put the game on ice. Moore this offseason to provide Josh Allen with a top wide receiver threat. But the star quarterback has traditionally leaned heavily on his tight ends for production through the air, and the opening week matchup proved this is not fully changing. Dalton Kincaid led all Bills’ pass catchers, pulling in five of his six targets for 130 total yards. Kincaid averaged 47.6 yards per game through the air last year, and has tallied 1,692 receiving yards through the first three years of his career. This is a great opportunity to build off this, as the Detroit Lions’ defense looked like it could be carved up by an adequate high school team in the season opener. The New Orleans Saints marched down the field with little resistance, putting up 469 total yards of offense and scoring 30 points in the matchup. This includes 378 yards through the air, and both tight ends were heavily involved in the attack. Juwan Johnson pulled in three receptions on seven targets for 54 yards and a touchdown, while Noah Fant added four receptions on eight targets for 33 yards and a score of his own The Bills lean on Kincaid at an even greater rate than the Saints do in their offensive attack, and he is a superior talent to the New Orleans tight ends. While the 130 yard output is not sustainable to repeat at a frequent rate, count on him remaining a key part of the gameplan and a safety valve for Allen throughout. Detroit should improve to some extent in their pass defense, but the matchup problem at the tight end position was evident in Week 1, and this is a difficult fix on a short week. Count on Kincaid remaining heavily involved in the Bills’ offense, and for over 50.5 receiving yards to be a comfortable bar to clear. Josh Allen Over 253.5 Passing Yards (-111) The 2024 NFL MVP got off to a strong start to this season, throwing for 334 yards on just 29 pass attempts against the Houston Texans. This is a Texans’ defense that finished last season ranked second in opponents’ points allowed, first in yards conceded, and sixth in opponents’ passing yards last season. They were widely expected to have a case for one of the top defensive units in football this year, but will need to make some major improvements from their Week 1 performance if this is to be the case. But the impressive output should say more about Allen than the Texans’ defense. The Bills’ star had a bit of a down season last year in his passing metrics, averaging 215.8 passing yards per game. But he is averaging 235.9 passing yards per game in his career and tallied as many as 284.0 over a season. Allen still tallied 253 passing yards or greater in seven games ,even with it being a down year in passing production last year. Allen will also be able to feast on this Lions’ defense, given the concerns mentioned above. Tyler Shough aired the ball out for 410 passing yards and three touchdowns against them last week to provide the upset scare. Even if you are not the biggest Allen fan, it is difficult to argue against the four-time Pro Bowler having significantly more arm talent than Shough. With better receiving talent around him and holes across this Detroit defense, expect plenty of passing success and for the 253.5 passing yard line not to be nearly high enough. For the sake of the article, we will stick to the standard passing prop, but some alternate lines also stand out for the Bills’ star, such as 280+ passing yards at +170 odds on DraftKings Sportsbook . Jahmyr Gibbs Over 90.5 Rushing Yards (-110) There is plenty of talent across this Lions’ offense, but it has become increasingly evident that Jahmyr Gibbs is the foundation of the attack. After splitting carries with David Montgomery to start his career, Detroit now leans on the Alabama product as their bell-cow back. Gibbs tallied a career-high and NFL-leading 29 carries in Week 1, turning these opportunities into 156 yards and two touchdowns. Buffalo holds plenty of defensive concerns of their own entering this matchup. In the opening week of the season, the Texans tallied 31 points and 381 total yards of offense against them. This includes 124 rushing yards on the ground, with former Lions standout Montgomery ripping off 60 yards and two touchdowns on his 20 carries while Woody Marks added 42 rushing yards of his own. Run defense was a concern for the Bills coming into the season, as they finished last year ranked 28th in the league in rushing yards allowed, 31st in rushing touchdowns conceded, and 30th in net yards per rush attempts. Gibbs has game-breaking speed and can take any given carry the length of the field for a touchdown score. With no real competition looking over his shoulder for carries, expect plenty of these chances and for the 24-year-old to find the open field at least once. He has tallied over 90.5 rushing yards in 13 games already in his career, and is receiving the largest opportunity in the offense thus far. Count on the Lions continuing to make it a clear effort to put the ball in the star running back’s hands and for Gibbs to have success against this porous defense. Back the Lions’ star to record over 90.5 rushing yards for the second straight week, and don’t be fully surprised if he exceeds last week’s massive 156 yard rushing output.
